name: Jump Nav
summary: A list of links into the page you are already on is the easiest navigation there is to build, and the one most likely to leave a keyboard reader exactly where they were. Whether following a link moves the keyboard at all comes down to one attribute on the thing it points at. Knowing which section you are in is the harder half.
demoNote: Examples 2 to 5 are live. Example 2 presses the same link into three documents one attribute apart and prints what took focus; example 3 measures the overlap between the heading and the bar stuck above it; example 4 counts scroll events against section changes on one document; example 5 prints the landmark menu two navs produce with and without names.
